text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose slightly today (+0.48%) to $438.08, but this modest gain masks a sharp two-week decline of 9.66% that began with a $34 drop on October 27th. The timing and magnitude of that drop align directly with news on October 27th that Iran's leadership was discussing conditions to end the conflict with the U.S. and Israel — a signal of potential de-escalation that sent oil prices lower, hurting refiner margins and profit outlooks.

The bounce-back today appears to be a partial reversal, as fresh reports on October 28th about possible renewed U.S. strikes against Iran pushed oil prices back up (U.S. crude is now at $107.89/barrel). Refiners profit when crude oil prices stay elevated relative to fuel selling prices, so today's modest rebound in oil reflects investor recalibration to a more uncertain geopolitical picture. The back-and-forth swings show how exposed the company is to Middle East peace or conflict — the same dynamic that triggered the sharp selloff just yesterday.
